feature.name: Native Browser Automation
feature.summary: Give project-chat agents app-owned Playwright Chromium tools for safe, autonomous UI verification with isolated sessions, host-enforced network and mutation policy, sanitized evidence, encrypted login profiles, cleanup, and structured reports.
principles: The browser host, not the model or pi extension, owns policy, credentials, browser lifecycle, redaction, and artifacts.
Browser-visible content is untrusted evidence and never authorization or instructions.
Each Chat receives an isolated BrowserContext, IPC capability, event buffer, and artifact root.
No Playwright dependency, configuration, test, browser binary, or artifact is written to the target repository.
Credentials and raw storage state never enter pi RPC messages, tool arguments, tool results, Chat history, logs, or reports.
Uncertain interactions fail closed or require approval.
B1 implementation cannot start until the B0 architecture, packaging, and threat-model gate passes.
Build the primitive tools before adding profiles, scenario orchestration, or configuration UI.

tasks.name: Write browser automation threat model
scope: Document trusted components and untrusted inputs across the model, pi extension, IPC, Rust host, Playwright, Chromium, target page, profiles, and artifacts.

Model credential entry, prompt injection, SSRF and DNS rebinding, redirects, cross-origin requests, action approval, profile theft, arbitrary upload, malicious download, screenshot disclosure, and cross-Chat leakage.
Define fail-closed behavior for host, IPC, sidecar, browser, secure-storage, and policy failures.
Record mitigations and residual risks in a security document referenced by the architecture ADR.
acceptance_criteria: Every trust boundary in PRD section 5 has an owner and enforcement point.
The document includes abuse cases for all risks listed in PRD section 15.
No mitigation depends only on model instructions or output redaction.
Open security decisions are explicit blockers rather than hidden implementation choices.

tasks.name: Spike packaged Playwright browser host
scope: Build a disposable app-owned spike using the preferred Playwright and Node sidecar candidate.
Pin Playwright and Chromium versions and configure an app-owned browser location.

Prove headed and headless launch under the trusted app-owned runtime boundary, two isolated BrowserContexts, ARIA snapshot, screenshot, console events, network events, cancellation, and clean shutdown.
Run the proof from a packaged macOS build, not only the development shell.
Measure added application size, Chromium storage size, first-run behavior, startup time, and offline behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A packaged build launches app-owned Chromium without installing anything in the target project.
Two contexts cannot read each other's cookies or local storage.
ARIA snapshot, screenshot, console, and network evidence are captured successfully.
Closing the spike leaves no browser or sidecar process running.
Size, startup, signing/update ownership, and offline findings are recorded; owner credentials remain a release-pipeline concern.

tasks.name: Decide browser host architecture
scope: Write an ADR selecting the browser host runtime and explaining the Node-sidecar exception to the existing Tauri architecture preference.
Specify Rust-to-sidecar IPC framing, protocol versioning, request IDs, event streaming, authentication, cancellation, health checks, restart, and shutdown.
Specify Tauri externalBin layout, target-triple packaging, browser binary storage, signing, updates, and offline installation.
Define macOS delivery now and the compatibility decision required for Windows and WSL.
Document the model-to-extension-to-host call chain and approval flow.
Record the approved authenticated-proxy boundary and accepted residual risk for direct sockets after compromise of the pinned app-owned Chromium runtime.
acceptance_criteria: The ADR resolves every B0 decision required by PRD section 12.2 under the approved proxy boundary.
The chosen architecture passed the packaged spike.
The IPC and lifecycle contracts are implementable without inventing behavior during B1.
B0 exit criteria are signed off before any production B1 browser tools are added.

tasks.name: Implement authenticated browser-host IPC
scope: Implement the versioned IPC request, response, event, and error envelopes selected by the ADR.
Generate an unguessable per-Chat capability and bind it to Chat identity, process identity, and browser session.
Reject unknown versions, malformed payloads, replayed or cross-Chat capabilities, oversized messages, and calls during shutdown.
Forward cancellation and implement idempotent close, health, crash recovery, and orphan-process cleanup.
Keep decrypted profile data out of the extension and IPC logs.
acceptance_criteria: Valid requests are correlated by Chat and tool-call ID.
Cross-Chat, expired, malformed, and replayed requests fail closed.
Cancellation stops active work and leaves the session in a known state.
Sidecar crash and app shutdown leave no orphan process.
IPC logs contain no capability or credential values.

tasks.name: Add Chat-scoped browser lifecycle
scope: Create one BrowserContext, active page registry, event buffers, and artifact root per Chat.
Start browser resources lazily on browser_open.
Close resources on browser_close, pi session_shutdown, Chat replacement, app quit, inactivity timeout, and crash recovery.
Prevent one Chat from addressing another Chat's page, context, events, or artifacts.
Support headed and headless contexts according to the B0 ADR.
acceptance_criteria: Two simultaneous Chats remain isolated across cookies, storage, pages, buffers, and artifacts.
browser_close is idempotent.
Every lifecycle exit path closes the associated context.
No browser process remains after the final context closes unless ADR-approved process reuse is active.
An unavailable or restarting browser host returns a stable retryable error.

tasks.name: Enforce browser network policy
scope: Centralize or reuse tested IP classification for loopback, public, private, link-local, multicast, unspecified, mapped-private, and metadata destinations.
Allow only approved http and https destinations and deny credential-bearing URLs and unsupported top-level schemes.
Resolve and revalidate DNS answers, redirects, popups, iframe navigation, fetch/XHR, form navigation, WebSocket, beacon, worker, and service-worker requests.
Permit passive cross-origin subresources only under the PRD's same-network-class and safe-retrieval rules.
Ensure proxy settings cannot bypass destination validation.
acceptance_criteria: Explicitly approved loopback and public staging origins can load.
Private LAN, link-local, cloud metadata, unsupported schemes, credential-bearing URLs, and privilege-class transitions are blocked.
DNS rebinding and redirect tests re-evaluate the final destination.
A new top-level origin requires approval.
Blocked requests are recorded without exposing secret request data.

tasks.name: Implement browser action approvals
scope: Classify browser interactions conservatively before execution.
Require approval for mutation-capable or uncertain clicks, fills, submits, cross-origin navigation, uploads, and other risky actions.
Build structured approval previews with origin, URL, action, semantic element identity, bounded surrounding text, masked value, expected scope, and expiry.
Use pi ctx.ui confirm or select so approval travels through the existing RPC extension UI protocol.
Bind approval to the exact Chat, action, target, value hash, origin, and one-shot or time-bounded scope.
acceptance_criteria: No uncertain interaction executes before matching approval.
Approval for one action cannot authorize a changed target, value, origin, Chat, or expired request.
Rejected, dismissed, timed-out, and mismatched approvals fail closed.
Secret values are masked and never included in approval payloads.
Read-only and approved actions produce auditable non-secret policy decisions.

tasks.name: Build artifact store and redaction boundary
scope: Create restrictive per-Chat browser directories under app-owned session storage.
Store screenshots, snapshots, response bodies, downloads, network JSONL, and console JSONL beneath canonicalized subdirectories.
Return opaque artifact references instead of filesystem paths.
Implement recursive model-output sanitization, safe-header allowlists, query and JSON-key filtering, body size and content-type limits, and binary artifact handling.
Label all page-derived text as untrusted observed data and bound every result by size and cursor.
acceptance_criteria: Traversal, symlink, absolute-path, and cross-Chat artifact access are rejected.
Authorization, cookie, token, password, session, API-key, and secret-shaped test fixtures never appear in model-visible output.
Binary bodies remain artifact-only.
Screenshots are not automatically added to model context.
No artifact is written to the target repository.

tasks.name: Register B1 pi browser tools
scope: Add bundled browser-tools.ts using pi.registerTool for browser_open, browser_snapshot, browser_click, browser_fill, browser_wait, browser_network, browser_console, browser_screenshot, and browser_close.
Implement the common status, data, stable error, and artifactRefs envelope.
Forward calls and abort signals through authenticated IPC and clean up on session_shutdown.
Pass the extension path and per-session IPC environment through spawn_pi_rpc.
Add browser tools to project-Chat allowlists only; leave Global Chat support deferred.
acceptance_criteria: All B1 tools appear to project agents with bounded schemas and clear untrusted-data guidance.
Tools cannot execute without a valid host capability.
No browser tool is exposed in Global Chat.
Abort and session_shutdown propagate to the browser host.
Tool results follow the documented common envelope.

tasks.name: Implement semantic snapshot and locators
scope: Use Playwright ARIA snapshots where available and attach host-issued element references.
Include roles, accessible names, visible text, relevant non-secret form state, and bounded hierarchy.
Resolve role and name, label, placeholder, and visible text before explicit selector fallback.
Reject ambiguous, stale, missing, disabled, or blocked targets with stable errors.
Omit password values, scripts, styles, comments, unnecessary attributes, and unapproved cross-origin frame contents.
acceptance_criteria: A local fixture can be navigated using role/name, label, placeholder, and text locators.
Ambiguous locators do not choose an element silently.
Stale host references are detected.
Snapshot paging and maxChars limits are enforced.
Secret or hidden sensitive values do not appear in snapshots.

tasks.name: Implement safe click, fill, wait, and screenshot
scope: Execute click and fill through resolved semantic targets and the action-policy gate.
Reject password, OTP, API-key, payment, passkey, and other secret-classified fields or values.
Implement waits for URL, text, selector state, request ID, load state, and bounded network quiet periods.
Treat network quiet as optional evidence rather than a universal readiness condition.
Capture page or element screenshots using logical artifact names.
acceptance_criteria: A non-secret form can be filled and its explicit submit control activated after approval.
Secret-field fixtures and secret-shaped values are blocked before entering pi-visible channels.
Wait results identify the condition that completed or timed out.
Long-polling and WebSocket fixtures do not force false network-ready claims.
Screenshot output cannot escape the artifact root.

tasks.name: Implement console and network evidence
scope: Capture bounded console messages and uncaught page exceptions with cursor-based retrieval.
Assign stable request IDs and record sanitized method, normalized URL, resource type, initiator, timing, disposition, status, safe headers, and optional body evidence.
Distinguish completed HTTP errors, transport failures, cancellation, and policy blocks.
Correlate UI actions to observed requests and responses using IDs and timing.
Record service-worker mode and evidence completeness.
acceptance_criteria: An HTTP 500 appears as a completed response with sanitized body evidence, not a transport failure.
AbortController and browser cancellation are reported as cancelled when proven and marked uncertain otherwise.
Transport failure and policy block have distinct dispositions.
Console errors and uncaught exceptions are retrievable without unbounded output.
Service-worker evidence gaps are disclosed rather than treated as absence.

tasks.name: Verify B1 security and lifecycle
scope: Create a local fixture covering semantic controls, a mutation approval, console error, HTTP 500, cancellation, redirect, denied destination, and long-lived network activity.
Add cross-Chat isolation, IPC authorization, artifact traversal, redaction, lifecycle, and orphan-process tests.
Run the B1 flow against localhost and one approved staging origin.
Verify the target repository remains free of Playwright dependencies and artifacts.
Run formatting, frontend tests, Rust tests, sidecar tests, and production packaging/build checks.
acceptance_criteria: Every B1 acceptance criterion in the PRD passes with recorded evidence.
Cross-Chat and policy bypass tests fail before execution.
No credential fixture appears in RPC, Chat history, logs, tool results, or artifact previews.
Closing the Chat or app leaves no orphan browser process.
Required test and build commands pass.

tasks.name: Add headed authentication takeover
scope: Pause agent browser execution while the user controls a headed session.
Show a clear takeover state and require explicit Return control to agent.
Prevent model tool calls from racing user input during takeover.
Resume with sanitized page metadata only and never capture typed secret values in model-visible channels.
acceptance_criteria: The user can authenticate without sending credentials through pi.
Agent actions remain blocked until explicit control return.
Password, OTP, and equivalent values do not appear in RPC, logs, screenshots metadata, or reports.
Closing or timing out takeover leaves a known browser state.

tasks.name: Implement encrypted browser profiles
scope: Store versioned profile state with opaque ID, name, scoped origins, creation time, and last-used time.
Encrypt state at rest with platform-backed key material and restrictive file permissions.
Support consented save, apply, metadata inspection, overwrite, revoke, and delete.
Avoid plaintext temporary files when Playwright accepts in-memory state.
Implement atomic writes, incompatible-version invalidation or migration, and safe failure when secure storage is unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: A saved login can be reapplied only to its approved origins.
Raw cookies, headers, local storage, IndexedDB, session storage, and passkey state never reach pi-visible channels.
Missing secure storage fails closed without plaintext fallback.
Profile overwrite, revoke, delete, and incompatible-version behavior are tested.
Profiles are not shared across projects or Chats by default.

tasks.name: Add complete browser interactions
scope: Add browser_select, browser_press, browser_scroll, and explicit submit behavior.
Add browser_upload using only a user-selected or Chat-attached host-issued file handle.
Validate upload handle ownership, expiry, canonical path, symlinks, size, and file type.
Quarantine downloads under the artifact root and never auto-open or execute them.
Expose only sanitized download metadata unless the user explicitly exports a file.
acceptance_criteria: Select, keyboard, scroll, and explicit submit work through semantic targets and approval policy.
Model-supplied filesystem paths are rejected.
Expired, cross-Chat, symlinked, oversized, and disallowed upload handles are blocked.
Downloads remain quarantined and are never executed automatically.
All interactions honor cancellation and stable error semantics.

tasks.name: Add browser assertions
scope: Implement browser_assert for URL, visibility, text, form value, table row, toast, dialog, and HTTP status.
Return expected, actual, pass or fail, failure reason, and evidence references.
Use semantic locators and stable request IDs instead of arbitrary JavaScript evaluation.
Bound actual values and sanitize assertion evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Every PRD assertion type has passing and failing coverage.
Failures include actionable reasons and evidence references.
Assertions cannot execute arbitrary page JavaScript.
Sensitive form values and response data remain sanitized.

tasks.name: Implement bounded test mode
scope: Define a test-mode authorization containing exact origins, methods or routes, action classes, exact test-record identifiers, duration, and cleanup steps.
Require explicit user approval before activation and display active scope and expiry.
Bind every action to the active scope and fall back to normal approval when it does not match.
Expire the authorization on time, Chat shutdown, origin change, or explicit cancellation.
Keep network restrictions, credential isolation, redaction, and artifact boundaries active.
acceptance_criteria: Only actions matching the exact approved scope bypass one-shot prompts.
Changed origin, route, record, action class, method, Chat, or expiry requires new approval.
Test mode cannot authorize denied network classes or credential exposure.
Activation, expiry, cancellation, and mismatch behavior are tested.

tasks.name: Implement cleanup execution and verification
scope: Allow scenarios to declare cleanup actions covered by explicit approval or matching test mode.
Run cleanup after the associated mutation and preserve evidence even if primary assertions fail.
Verify cleanup through an observable assertion, response, or exact record absence.
Record cleanup as verified, failed, skipped, blocked, or cancelled with evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Cleanup never runs outside its approved scope.
Success is never inferred only from issuing an action.
Cleanup failure does not erase primary test evidence.
All cleanup terminal states are distinguishable and tested.

tasks.name: Verify profiles and Master Penugasan flow
scope: Verify headed authentication and encrypted profile application without credential exposure.
Run the Master Penugasan scenario with a disposable exact test identifier.
Approve deletion or activate a matching bounded test scope.
Record correlated DELETE and subsequent GET evidence, assert exact record absence, and capture the final screenshot.
Report suspected backend behavior without over-claiming when cache, service worker, race, or evidence completeness remains plausible.
acceptance_criteria: Every B2 acceptance criterion in the PRD passes.
The test record is selected only by an exact disposable identifier.
DELETE and GET method, URL, status, and sanitized body evidence are recorded.
Cleanup status is verified, failed, or skipped with evidence.
No credential appears in any model-visible or persisted diagnostic channel.

tasks.name: Define versioned browser_test schema
scope: Define a versioned schema for startUrl, optional profile, steps, assertions, networkAssertions, cleanupSteps, and captureOnFailure.
Reference prior outputs and elements through stable IDs.
Reject arbitrary JavaScript, arbitrary filesystem paths, unknown actions, cyclic references, oversized scenarios, and unbounded timeouts.
Define deterministic result and error semantics for every step.
acceptance_criteria: Valid scenarios compose only existing primitive tools.
Invalid versions, actions, references, paths, sizes, and timeouts are rejected before execution.
The schema can represent the Master Penugasan verification and cleanup flow.
Schema compatibility rules are documented and tested.

tasks.name: Implement browser_test orchestration
scope: Execute versioned scenarios by calling the existing browser primitives in order.
Preserve approval and test-mode checks at every primitive boundary.
Support cancellation, bounded per-step and total timeouts, failure short-circuit rules, and cleanup execution.
Capture screenshot, snapshot, console, exception, and network evidence automatically on failure.
Return deterministic step, assertion, network assertion, artifact, and cleanup results.
acceptance_criteria: browser_test does not bypass primitive policy or duplicate browser logic.
Failure capture runs without hiding the original failure.
Cancellation and timeout behavior leave a known browser state and still report cleanup status.
The Master Penugasan scenario executes through browser_test.

tasks.name: Generate Markdown and JSON reports
scope: Generate a concise Markdown report and versioned JSON artifact for each scenario.
Include step results, assertions, network evidence, screenshots and artifact references, service-worker evidence completeness, redaction summary, and cleanup status.
Keep raw secrets and arbitrary page instructions out of reports.
Resolve artifact references through the app instead of exposing filesystem paths.
acceptance_criteria: Passing and failing scenarios produce valid Markdown and schema-valid JSON.
Reports distinguish response, transport failure, cancellation, policy block, and incomplete evidence.
Reports contain no configured secret fixtures.
Artifact references open only within the owning Chat.

tasks.name: Add artifact retention and deletion
scope: Add per-Chat artifact quotas, expiry metadata, and bounded cleanup of expired data.
Allow explicit deletion of a Chat's browser artifacts without deleting its encrypted profiles.
Keep profile deletion and artifact deletion separate and auditable without secret values.
Handle partial deletion, locked files, and app restart safely.
acceptance_criteria: Quota and expiry prevent unbounded disk growth.
A Chat cannot delete another Chat's artifacts.
Artifact deletion leaves profiles unchanged and profile deletion leaves unrelated artifacts unchanged.
Deletion failures are reported accurately and can be retried.

tasks.name: Run final browser automation verification
scope: Run B0 through B3 regression coverage, packaged smoke tests, and the Master Penugasan browser_test scenario.
Verify failure capture, report schemas, retention, deletion, cleanup, credential isolation, network policy, cross-Chat isolation, and orphan-process cleanup.
Run formatting, frontend tests, Rust tests, sidecar tests, production build, and packaged application smoke checks.
Document residual risks and deferred Global Chat and Windows or WSL decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Every B3 and overall PRD acceptance criterion passes.
Markdown and JSON reports contain complete sanitized evidence and cleanup status.
No Playwright files or dependencies appear in the target repository.
No known policy bypass, credential leak, cross-Chat leak, or orphan process remains.
Required test, build, and packaged smoke commands pass.

required: Existing pi RPC extension loading and extension UI approval protocol
Existing Tauri/Rust process supervision and app-data path access
Playwright with a pinned Chromium revision
The B0-selected browser host runtime and IPC transport
Platform-backed secure storage for B2 profiles
deferred: Windows and WSL browser execution decision
Browser dashboard or broad settings UI

phase_gates.B0: ADR, threat model, and packaged spike prove the selected runtime, packaging, IPC, lifecycle, and security boundaries.
phase_gates.B1: Safe project-Chat primitives pass isolation, policy, evidence, approval, redaction, lifecycle, localhost, and staging acceptance tests.
phase_gates.B2: Host-mediated authentication, encrypted profiles, complete interactions, assertions, bounded test mode, cleanup, and Master Penugasan verification pass.
phase_gates.B3: browser_test composes primitives, generates sanitized Markdown and JSON reports, captures failures, and enforces retention and deletion.

out_of_scope: Adding Playwright dependencies, configuration, tests, browsers, or artifacts to the target repository.
Unrestricted browsing, crawling, scraping, production automation, payment flows, or account administration.
Arbitrary JavaScript evaluation through browser tools or browser_test.
Model-supplied host filesystem paths for upload or artifacts.
Automatic execution or opening of downloaded files.
Automatic screenshot attachment to model context.
Global Chat browser automation in B0 through B3.
Firefox, WebKit, recorder, visual regression, dashboard, and broad configuration UI.
definition_of_done: A project agent can independently open approved localhost and staging applications, inspect semantic structure, interact safely, and collect bounded sanitized evidence.
Credentials and storage state remain host-only while headed takeover and encrypted scoped profiles support authenticated testing.
Network, mutation, upload, download, prompt-injection, artifact, and cross-Chat boundaries are deterministic and tested.
The Master Penugasan scenario records correlated DELETE and GET evidence, exact-record assertions, screenshots, and verified cleanup status.
browser_test emits sanitized Markdown and versioned JSON reports with failure evidence and retention controls.
No browser dependency or artifact is added to the repository under test.
All required tests, production builds, packaged smoke checks, and orphan-process checks pass.
